title: Staggered model onboarding — GPU reserve & KV sensitivity (worksheet)
body:
Purpose: working worksheet to size GPU reserves and KV cache impact for a staggered multi-region rollout of two new model variants (gptx-7B and gptx-13B-quant). This doc captures assumptions, sensitivity to KV hit-rate and average sequence lengths, and an allocation proposal for reserved vs. spot capacity in NA, EU, and APAC.

Background: planning team asked for a low-friction rollout with safety capacity baked in to avoid cross-customer noisy-neighbor regressions. Key constraints: (1) limited dedicated GPUs in APAC until Q1-2026, (2) cost target of <0.65 $/k-token for high-throughput routes, (3) ability to immediately scale down pre-warmed kernels if usage is low.

High-level approach: stagger regional rollouts in three waves (NA -> EU -> APAC), maintain a 25% guaranteed GPU reserve for canary/pinned traffic, and use spot/ephemeral capacity for burst traffic above baseline. KV cache is sharded by model+region; we model slice sizes and eviction sensitivity to estimate peak host RAM needs.

Assumptions (conservative base):
- gptx-7B: 12 tokens/sec per GPU (continuous throughput with batching), KV slice per concurrent session = 0.14 GB (avg seq_len=512).
- gptx-13B-quant (INT8): 8 tokens/sec per GPU, KV slice per concurrent session = 0.22 GB (avg seq_len=768).
- Baseline QPS at rollout start: NA=250 r/s, EU=120 r/s, APAC=60 r/s. 25% of requests are long-context (>1k tokens) which increase KV slice linearly.
- Target reserve pool per region = max(25% of steady-state GPUs, 4 GPUs) for safety.
- KV hit-rate scenarios: Low=35% hit, Base=60% hit, High=85% hit. Lower hit -> higher per-request KV reads and more memory churn due to misses leading to more cache population and transient duplication.

Sensitivity analysis summary (narrative):
- KV hit-rate has an outsized effect on host RAM and transient bandwidth requirements but only modest effect on raw GPU-hours (unless misses cause repeated re-computation or longer seqs).
- Longer average sequence lengths (1.5x) increase per-session KV footprint proportionally; plan for worst-case region memory = base footprint * 1.5.
- Spot capacity is cheap for bursty traffic if pre-warm penalty is acceptable; reserve pool must be able to handle the first 10 minutes of a region-level surge while spot autoscale warms new nodes.

Key computed outputs (see table_rows below for numeric scenarios):
- Reserve GPUs suggested: NA 40 (25% reserve applied to planned steady demand + 4 buffer), EU 18, APAC 10. Reserve counts include kernel pre-warms for canary traffic (2 GPUs per new model variant in region).
- Estimated KV resident memory under Base hit-rate: NA 4.6 TB, EU 2.2 TB, APAC 1.1 TB. Under Low hit-rate these increase by ~1.6x due to sharded duplication during population windows.
- Estimated incremental GPU-hours/week (both models active): NA ~18.9k, EU ~8.5k, APAC ~3.7k (sensitivity +/- 20% depending on batching efficiency).

Operational mitigations recommended:
- Staggered ramp schedule: Week 0 (NA canary 10% traffic), Week 2 (NA full), Week 3 (EU canary 15%), Week 5 (EU full), Week 6 (APAC canary 20%), Week 8 (APAC full).
- Implement KV slice cap per session with graceful degrade after N concurrent sessions to limit peak host memory. Cap defaults: gptx-7B 1.5k tokens, gptx-13B-quant 2k tokens.
- Pre-warm policy: keep 2 pre-warmed GPUs per model per region in reserve during canary and first-week full rollout; scale down based on observed kernel reuse rate (<30% reuse over 30m -> scale down).
- Canary traffic routing: use dedicated route with double-logging to compare outputs and collect KV efficacy metrics (hit-rate, eviction churn).

Open questions / data needed:
- Real telemetry for average sequence length per customer route (we have per-tenant histograms but need route-level breakdowns).
- Exact kernel memory residency numbers for gptx-13B-quant in APAC hardware (some hosts use different HBM configurations).
- SLA decision for warm-up failure modes (if pre-warm fails, do we route to a cheaper model automatically?).

Next steps / owners:
- SRE (Noah Kim): run stress test sim for low-hit kv scenario using synthetic workloads (deadline 2026-02-25).
- Applied ML infra (Miguel Santos): collect route-level seq_len histograms and publish into onboarding dashboard (deadline 2026-02-20).
- Product (Aisha Patel): sign off on staged ramp dates and safety thresholds (deadline 2026-02-18).

Notes: keep this worksheet as the single source of truth for allocation numbers until the Post-Mortem after ramp completes. Update the sheet_rows block below after simulations and replace conservative assumptions with measured numbers.
